title: Project Total Value
prompt: A TypeScript summary receives projects with numeric values. Write a typed function that returns the sum of all value fields.

explanation.beginner:
Example: projectTotalValue([{"value":3},{"value":7}]) produces 10. Choose the numeric contribution of each record, then combine those contributions using the contract’s initial value.

Compare “returns zero for no values”: input [[]] produces 0. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Choose the numeric contribution of each record, then combine those contributions using the contract’s initial value.

Tempting mistake: A count of records is not a sum of their values. Test empty input and a zero-valued record separately.

The reference uses reduce. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “returns zero for no values”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
